chunks: [A part of the same sermon on innovation (bid‘ah) :]
No innovation is introduced unless one sunnah is forsaken, keep away from innovations and stick to the broad road. Surely the old tested ways are the best and the innovated ones are bad.

key_terms.الْمَهْيَعُ: The broad road or clear path
key_terms.بِدْعَةٌ: Innovation (bid'ah), a newly introduced matter in religion
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: Sunnah, the established tradition or practice of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between religious innovation (bid'ah) and the prophetic tradition (sunnah) according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) establishes a direct causal link between religious innovation (bid'ah) and the erosion of prophetic tradition (sunnah), a concept central to Shia jurisprudential methodology for preserving authentic practice. By urging adherence to the 'clear path' (al-mahya), he emphasizes that stability in established norms is superior to the novelty of new inventions, which are often characterized as the worst of matters. This dichotomy reflects the broader Shia emphasis on returning to the source of revelation and the Ahl al-Bayt's understanding of it, rather than relying on later, potentially divergent, scholarly innovations.
